title: Crusoe email to Callaway Commissioners: 53% effective abatement rate calculation, $5.7B total tax estimate
author: Lucas Workman
notes:
Lucas Workman (Crusoe) to the Callaway County Commissioners, cc Heather Tazalla, Conor Bates-Janigo, Curt Warfield, Gary Jungermann. Thanks the Commissioners for their willingness to keep communicating and partnering toward an agreeable solution, and attaches Crusoe's calculation for a 53% effective overall abatement rate (the "effective rate" tab), assuming a 25-year term at 0% abatement on real property and 85% abatement on personal property, $95.55M in CBA payments, and the fire and ambulance district opting out of the Chapter 100 abatement. Under these assumptions, Crusoe states the project will still generate an estimated $5.7B in total tax revenue for the county's taxing entities over the 25-year term.

How the 53% figure is likely derived: it is not a simple average of 0% and 85%, but a weighted rate. Real property and personal property each have a baseline tax liability over the 25 years if fully taxed; applying 0% abatement to real property leaves it fully taxed, while applying 85% abatement to personal property reduces personal property tax collected to 15% of baseline. The fire and ambulance district opting out means it collects its full share regardless, outside the abatement calculation. The effective rate is the total abated (foregone) tax across both categories divided by what would have been collected with no abatement at all - so the 53% depends heavily on the underlying split between real property value and personal property value in the project, since personal property carries by far the larger abatement.

Open question worth tracking: how much of the projected $5.7B is real estate tax versus personal property tax. Personal property is where the abatement actually applies, and it is also the value most likely to shrink over the 25-year term, since data center hardware becomes cheaper and denser over time and would likely be reassessed at lower value or replaced - meaning the real effective abatement rate could rise well above 53% as the equipment underlying the personal property valuation ages and depreciates faster than real estate does.
